## Claims
- [source-backed] The 2011 paper treats minimality of the two Theorem 5.4 generating sets as a conjecture, while it separately presents \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\) as a stronger suspected statement. [source-6, lines 56-72]
- [source-backed] The 2024 candidate’s supplied abstract states only: “We prove the minimality conjecture.” [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832]
- [proved] A free integral indecomposables statement \(J/\Lambda_+J\cong\mathbb Z^N\), with the specified \(N\) generators mapping to a basis, implies their minimality; the converse does not establish torsion-freeness or identify \(J/\Lambda_+J\) as \(\mathbb Z^N\).
- [unsupported] No bounded 2024 full-text passage with stable theorem locator, hypotheses, or coefficient-ring statement was supplied; therefore applicability of the 2024 theorem to the present integral \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) is unverified.

## Strategy
Separate the abstract-level 2024 minimality lead from the stronger quotient assertion, using the elementary quotient implication above.

## Gaps
The required 2024 full-text source-refresh certificate cannot be executed from the supplied materials: no citable FULL-TEXT SOURCE block for DOI `10.1112/jlms.12832` is available.

## Next
Requested target established: **no**. The missing bounded 2024 theorem text must supply its exact statement, hypotheses, and locators before the minimality theorem can be source-grounded; it would still not by itself establish the stronger integral indecomposables statement.
